text:
[LNUL.5.3] **Coalesce `??`.** `x ?? d` (with `d : T`) has type `T`: yields `x`
when non-null, else `d`. Restores opt-in old behaviour explicitly, e.g.
`cached("k") ?? ""` when an author genuinely wants empty-string-on-miss. The dimensions of `x` and
`d` are [LUNI.8.8]'s.

A fault is not `null` ([LNUL.4.2]). When evaluating `x` faults, the expression
yields that fault, and the engine **must not** evaluate `d`: `??` stands in for
an absent value, never for a failed computation.

idris.name: lnul_5_3__coalesce
idris.note: x when it has a value that is not null, else d, over the fragment's values; d is passed unevaluated, so the type's own order is [LNUL.8.9]'s.

idris.name: lnul_5_3__null_takes_the_default
idris.note: A null takes the default for every default: its value, or its trap.

idris.name: lnul_5_3__trap_has_no_fallback
idris.note: A trap in x is the answer for every default, as the clause's last paragraph states; formal/k/dsexpr.k's `trap ?? _ => trap` is the same rule.

idris.name: lnul_8_9__default_not_looked_at
idris.note: For every value that is not null and every default, a trapping one included, x ?? d is x.
